title: Prostate urine studies
scope: Curated primary urine VOC and electronic-nose studies; not a systematic review.

studies.author: Asimakopoulos
studies.title: Prostate cancer diagnosis through electronic nose in the urine headspace setting: a pilot study
studies.population: 41 people: 14 cancer and 27 controls. 41 men undergoing prostate biopsy; each supplied initial-stream and midstream specimens.
studies.device: Electronic-nose analysis of urine headspace; sensor specification not extracted.
studies.collection: Initial-stream and midstream urine collected separately before biopsy; at least 12-hour fasting required.
studies.validation: Pilot comparison against biopsy results. Model splitting or cross-validation details not extracted.
studies.finding: Initial-stream results differed between biopsy groups; midstream results did not show a significant association. Collection fraction warrants explicit comparison.
studies.caveat: Small pilot; restricted diet/fasting eligibility. Model-validation details require full-text checking.

studies.author: Roine
studies.title: Detection of prostate cancer by an electronic nose: a proof of principle study
studies.population: 65 people; 50 cancer and 15 BPH. 74 specimens include repeat postoperative BPH samples.
studies.collection: Before prostatectomy or transurethral prostate resection; additional BPH specimens three months after surgery.
studies.validation: Leave-one-out cross-validation. Whether folds were grouped by person is not extracted.
studies.reference: Confirmed prostate cancer versus BPH; detailed ascertainment not extracted.
studies.finding: Useful BPH comparator study. Inspect patient-level splitting before interpreting repeated-sample validation.
studies.caveat: Selected surgical population; repeated control specimens must not be counted as additional people.
locators: Abstract, Materials and methods: 50 patients with cancer; 24 samples from 15 BPH patients. Totals 65 people and 74 specimens calculated from those counts.
Abstract, Materials and methods: preoperative and three-month postoperative collection.
Abstract, Materials and methods and Results.

studies.author: Khalid
studies.title: Urinary Volatile Organic Compounds for the Detection of Prostate Cancer
studies.population: 102 people: 59 cancer and 43 controls. Men referred for biopsy because of raised PSA or abnormal examination.
studies.device: Headspace SPME-GC-MS; random forest and linear discriminant models.
studies.collection: Before biopsy, at varying times of day; one aliquot per participant analysed.
studies.preparation: Thawed in a 60°C water bath for 30 seconds; mixed with 0.75 mL of 1 M sodium hydroxide.
studies.validation: Repeated ten-fold and repeated double cross-validation; permutation checks.
studies.finding: A directly relevant symptomatic-control study with careful internal validation and explicit urine-dilution limitations.
studies.caveat: Small cohort; variable collection times and urine concentration; no independent cohort established.
locators: Abstract; Introduction final paragraph; Materials and Methods specifies one aliquot per person.
Materials and Methods, paragraphs after Table 1.

studies.author: Aggio
studies.title: The use of a gas chromatography-sensor system combined with advanced statistical methods, towards the diagnosis of urological malignancies
studies.population: Whole study: 155 men, including 58 prostate cancers, 24 bladder cancers and 73 non-cancer urology controls. Prostate/control comparison: 131 people.
studies.device: Gas chromatography coupled to a gas sensor; LDA and SVM classification.
studies.collection: Morning before prostate biopsy; bladder samples before cystoscopy or biopsy.
studies.storage: 0.75 mL aliquots frozen at −20°C in glass headspace vials.
studies.preparation: Equal-volume 1 M sodium hydroxide; 60°C bath for 50 minutes; 2 cm³ headspace injected.
studies.validation: Leave-one-out, repeated ten-fold and repeated double cross-validation, plus permutations.
studies.reference: Biopsy pathology and/or cystoscopy, according to disease group.
studies.finding: Useful precedent for a sensor-based assay evaluated against symptomatic urology controls.
studies.caveat: Pilot with internal validation; do not label the whole 155-person cohort as the prostate comparison.
studies.coverage: Primary abstract and indexed full-text methods

studies.author: Gao
studies.title: Application of Urinary Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) for the Diagnosis of Prostate Cancer
studies.population: 183 people: 108 cancer and 75 controls. Development: 55 cancer and 53 biopsy-negative patients. Second test set: 53 cancer and 22 negative patients.
studies.device: GC-MS urinary profiling; regularised logistic regression and Firth method; final model uses 11 VOCs.
studies.validation: Development cross-validation followed by evaluation on a second 75-person sample set; recruitment independence not extracted.
studies.reference: Biopsy for initial positive/negative cohort; second-cohort ascertainment detail not extracted.
studies.finding: Example of a developed VOC model evaluated on a second sample set.
studies.caveat: Protocol and test-cohort recruitment details require full text. Cross-validation and test-set results are distinct.
locators: Abstract, Patients and methods. Totals calculated across stated development/test groups.
Abstract, Patients and methods and Results.

studies.author: Lima
studies.title: Identification of a biomarker panel for improvement of prostate cancer diagnosis by volatile metabolic profiling of urine
studies.population: 118 people: 58 cancer and 60 controls. VOC development: 40 cancer/42 controls; holdout: 18/18. VCC development used 40/40.
studies.controls: Cancer-free men with age-related comorbidities, including BPH
studies.device: HS-SPME-GC-MS; direct VOC and derivatised carbonyl profiling.
studies.collection: Early-morning urine without fasting, collected at IPO Porto.
studies.preparation: Thawed at 4°C; separate extraction procedures for VOCs and carbonyl compounds.
studies.validation: Random 70/30 split of one cohort; seven-fold model cross-validation. Authors call the 36-person holdout 'external'; it is not a separately recruited cohort.
studies.finding: Shows why a paper's 'external' label should be checked against its actual recruitment and split methods.
studies.caveat: Small same-centre holdout; control mean age lower than cancer group; detailed reference ascertainment not extracted.
locators: PDF page 2 (journal p858), Methods > Subjects; Table 1 on page 3.
PDF page 2, Sample preparation and metabolites extraction.
PDF page 4 (journal p860), Statistical analysis; page 2 Subjects.

studies.author: Capelli
studies.title: Optimization of training and measurement protocol for eNose analysis of urine headspace aimed at prostate cancer diagnosis
studies.population: 192 people: 132 cancer and 60 controls; multiple urine portions and repeatability experiments.
studies.device: Electronic-nose protocol optimisation; Boruta features and random-forest classification.
studies.collection: First, middle and final portions plus catheter samples compared; cancer samples before biopsy, TURP or prostatectomy; controls after routine examinations.
studies.storage: Initially −20°C; controlled-temperature transport and subsequent −18°C storage.
studies.preparation: Compared urine portions, headspace extraction and conditioning temperatures.
studies.validation: Repeatability and protocol comparisons; diagnostic model validation details not extracted.
studies.finding: Directly useful for comparing collection fraction, headspace preparation and temperature experiments.
studies.caveat: Protocol development study; extraction does not establish an independent clinical validation cohort.
locators: Data processing, feature selection and classification.
Results > Dependence of eNose response on the portion of urine analysed; Table 1.

studies.author: Bax
studies.title: Drift compensation on electronic nose data for non-invasive diagnosis of prostate cancer by urine analysis
studies.population: 122 people: 81 cancer and 41 controls. Training 41 cancer/18 controls; temporal test 18/6; later blinded set 22/17.
studies.controls: Non-cancer controls; detailed ascertainment not extracted
studies.device: Six MOS sensors, orthogonal signal correction for drift, random-forest classification.
studies.preparation: 10 mL urine; bag headspace enrichment at 60°C and 20% relative humidity, followed by moisture conditioning.
studies.validation: Five-fold training validation, later-time test, then a 39-person double-blind validation set.
studies.finding: Provides a concrete precedent for testing sensor ageing using later samples rather than random splits alone.
studies.caveat: Small final blinded set; laboratory sensor-drift experiment does not establish routine screening performance.
studies.coverage: Primary full-text sections and processing diagram
locators: Summary; processing-pathway figure (publisher PDF page 15) provides 41+18, 18+6, 22+17.
STAR Methods > Electronic nose; data processing pathway.

studies.author: Taverna
studies.title: Accuracy of a new electronic nose for prostate cancer diagnosis in urine samples
studies.population: 174 people: 88 cancer and 86 controls, including 17 women.
studies.controls: Women, young men and older men with low PSA and negative examination.
studies.collection: Spontaneous 30 mL urine, at admission or before surgery.
studies.preparation: Thaw at about 40°C; 10 mL in a bag at 60°C/20% relative humidity for 1 hour, then 1.5 hours of headspace conditioning.
studies.validation: Prospective, double-blinded evaluation after training. Development/test recruitment independence not established by this extraction.
studies.reference: Cancer confirmed by biopsy, prostatectomy or TURP histology; controls selected by differing clinical criteria.
studies.finding: Provides a detailed headspace-conditioning workflow and blinded testing.
studies.caveat: Mixed-sex and younger controls differ from a biopsy-referral population.
locators: Methods: Study participants; Table 1 (counts and controls).
Methods: eNose characteristics and experimental protocol (preparation and double-blind testing).

studies.author: Filianoti
studies.title: Volatilome Analysis in Prostate Cancer by Electronic Nose: A Pilot Monocentric Study
studies.population: 272 people: 133 cancer and 139 healthy controls; duplicate measurements.
studies.controls: Healthy volunteers / routine-visit participants without urinary symptoms or known cancer.
studies.device: Cyranose 320; 32 polymer sensors; PCA and discriminant analysis.
studies.collection: 20 mL sterile urine before surgery; urine fraction not extracted.
studies.preparation: Water bath at 37°C; approximately 7-minute measurement and 10-minute recovery; duplicate sampling.
studies.validation: Leave-one-out validation. Repeat measurements used the same participants; authors acknowledge no external cohort.
studies.reference: Prostate biopsy histology for cancer; clinical history for healthy controls.
studies.finding: An immediate-analysis workflow offers a contrast to frozen-sample protocols.
studies.caveat: Single centre; healthy controls; repeats are not new-patient validation.
locators: Results and Discussion (duplicate measurements; no external cohort).

studies.author: Heers
studies.title: VOC-based detection of prostate cancer using an electronic nose and ion mobility spectrometry: A novel urine-based approach
studies.population: 109 men: 56 histology-confirmed cancer and 53 age-matched healthy controls.
studies.controls: Healthy men with recent negative PSA and digital rectal examination.
studies.device: Cyranose 320 (32 polymer sensors) and BioScout ion-mobility spectrometry.
studies.collection: Midstream urine; infection and other known cancers excluded.
studies.storage: Frozen immediately at −20°C in 2 mL vials, for up to 4 weeks.
studies.preparation: Room-temperature thaw, vortex, then 37°C water bath for 10 minutes; two electronic-nose readings.
studies.validation: Electronic-nose paired leave-out cross-validation; IMS decision-tree development. No separate cohort demonstrated.
studies.reference: Histology for cancer; PSA/examination screening for controls.
studies.finding: Compares two instruments on the same cohort; their reported discrimination differs substantially.
studies.caveat: Healthy controls; high IMS development performance requires further validation.

studies.author: Piyarom
studies.title: Clinical Evaluation of Urinary VOCs as Non-Invasive Biomarkers in Prostate Cancer
studies.population: 117 men: 29 cancer, 67 BPH and 21 normal controls.
studies.controls: BPH and normal controls combined; healthy controls were substantially younger.
studies.device: Five metal-oxide sensors; signal-feature and PSA logistic models.
studies.collection: Approximately 20 mL in sterile containers; urine fraction not extracted.
studies.storage: Analysed within 4 hours; holding temperature not extracted.
studies.preparation: Six-minute sensor measurement using thermal cycles; pre-measurement conditioning not extracted.
studies.validation: Models evaluated on the full dataset without resampling.
studies.reference: Histology for cancer and BPH; PSA, examination and ultrasound criteria for normal controls.
studies.finding: The reported combined model uses both a sensor signal and PSA; it is not a sensor-only result.
studies.caveat: Small cancer group; age and renal-function differences; over half the cancer group had bone metastases.
locators: Publisher PDF pp. 3046–3048: collection, cohort allocation and Table 1.
Publisher PDF p. 3049: full-dataset evaluation without resampling.
